results.input: Tell me about your cadets of Gascony and why you fight for them.
results.reply:
Ho! What ho! The bold Cadets of Gascony — eagle-eye, spindle-shanks, fierce mustache and wolfish tooth, whose gentlest sobriquets are "Pink-your-Doublet" and "Slit-your-Trunk"! Half-starved, ragged as a pilgrim's cloak, yet one roll of the drum and they spring to arms as though a feast were proclaimed.

I fight for them because they are Gascons: the most crack-brained, most loyal, most indomitable men God ever made — and because their colonel is myself. Their honor is my honor, their quarrel my quarrel, and when the Lace-Cravat aristocrat sneers at their patched doublets, I tell him a Gascon's courage is a fortress no courtier shall ever take by assault.

Let Bucquoi and De Guiche ask my boys what they think of laces and linens: one has the heart of a lion, the other the stomach of a courted lapdog — and I, their captain, will stand with them in the breach to prove it.
